q: Waves are classified as transverse and longitudinal waves depending on vibration of particles in the medium through which they propagate.
e: True. Waves are classified as transverse and longitudinal waves depending on vibration of particles in the medium through which they propagate. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound.

q: If the displacements of particles of the medium are perpendicular to the direction of the wave, such a wave is called a transverse wave.
e: True. If the displacements of particles of the medium are perpendicular to the direction of the wave, such a wave is called a transverse wave. In a transverse wave the particles shake at right angles to the travel.

q: If the displacements of particles of the medium are parallel to the direction of the wave, such a wave is called a transverse wave.
e: False. If the displacements of particles of the medium are perpendicular to the direction of the wave, such a wave is called a transverse wave. This claim used parallel in place of perpendicular.

q: Waves in a vibrating string are transverse waves.
e: True. Waves in a vibrating string are transverse waves. In a transverse wave the particles shake at right angles to the travel.

q: Light waves and other electromagnetic waves are also transverse waves.
e: True. Light waves and other electromagnetic waves are also transverse waves. In a transverse wave the particles shake at right angles to the travel.

q: If the displacements of particles of medium are parallel to the direction of the waves, such a wave is called a longitudinal wave.
e: True. If the displacements of particles of medium are parallel to the direction of the waves, such a wave is called a longitudinal wave. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound.

q: Compressional waves in a slinky coiled spring and sound waves are longitudinal waves.
e: True. Compressional waves in a slinky coiled spring and sound waves are longitudinal waves. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound.

q: A longitudinal wave is demonstrated by rapidly pushing forth and pulling back at one end of a slinky coiled spring while another end is fixed.
e: True. A longitudinal wave is demonstrated by rapidly pushing forth and pulling back at one end of a slinky coiled spring while another end is fixed. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound.

q: It can be seen that the back and forth movement of the coil is perpendicular to the wave direction.
e: False. It can be seen that the back and forth movement of the coil is parallel to the wave direction. This claim used perpendicular in place of parallel.

q: It can be seen that the back and forth movement of the coil is parallel to the wave direction.
e: True. It can be seen that the back and forth movement of the coil is parallel to the wave direction. It can be seen that the back and forth movement of the coil is parallel to the wave direction is a travelling disturbance that carries energy, not the medium itself.

q: Some waves in nature exhibit a combination of transverse and longitudinal waves.
e: True. Some waves in nature exhibit a combination of transverse and longitudinal waves. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound.

q: Water waves are good example of combinational waves.
e: True. Water waves are good example of combinational waves. Every quantity named in that sentence is being used in its physics sense.
